meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: Leucine binds a pocket inside Sestrin2 with roughly 20 uM affinity - close to the concentration at which cells actually feel leucine coming and going. The bound sensor can no longer hold GATOR2, so leucine effectively switches the brake off.
data.mechanism_beginner: Leucine sticks to a pocket inside Sestrin2 and makes it let go of the next protein in line – that's how the cell notices leucine is around.
data.boundary: Affinity was measured in vitro; whether the same 20 uM setpoint holds in tissues with different leucine transport is untested.
